page: Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the Dalv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 8.0 GB of system memory, which equates to a low-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, falls within the average range. However, memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the PassMark memory score is in the bottom 10%, and read-only memory bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA-NI instructions, yielding average performance in encryption tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a budget-friendly entry point for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. Due to the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and weak memory bandwidth, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale compilation. It is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, text processing, and basic microservices.
